title: Cube-root parity bridge for Goldbach
objective: Investigate whether the signed cube-root rough-pair statistic can be bounded strictly below zero for every sufficiently large even target, and independently challenge every proposed proof step, source dependency, and finite extrapolation.
deliverables: Exact definitions and proof of the finite signed identity with reflection, boundary and parity handling
A parameter-uniform candidate estimate, its conditional consequences and complete dependency map
A source-inspected comparison with Huang and Li, rough numbers and OpenAI mathematics
Independent critic seeking counterexamples and revealing hidden circularity or parity assumptions
Preregistered exact arithmetic finite checks and separate reproducible results
Execution mode, resource receipt, unresolved obligations and explicitly marked next steps
success_criteria: Only an actual proof with explicit hypotheses can be labeled proved; computational observations never establish an unbounded theorem
The unrestricted fixed-percentage Chen gap is recognized as false and the roughness transition is respected
Ordinary Liouville cancellation is not falsely assumed at the cubic cutoff
A pointwise theorem is not inferred from an average theorem or positive-density result
The author and critic are distinct profiles and each conclusion has provenance and independent review
No purported universal bound silently assumes Goldbach or an equivalent positivity result
stop_conditions: One bounded round and 30 proxy dispatch units; no nested or unbounded feedback
Stop at a missing pointwise estimate and preserve the gap as open
No paid provider calls without explicitly configured authorized provider and budget
No publication, push, external message or external mutable action by workers
Treat proof-checker failures and missing dependencies as unverified rather than asserting success
